items.title: Tensor-product NURBS patch maps and rational spline spaces
items.statement: Defines tensor-product B-spline numerators on a parameter box, positive rational weights, the NURBS denominator and basis, the geometry map, and piecewise C1 bi-Lipschitz patch admissibility with positive cell Jacobians and explicit derivative and inverse bounds.
items.strategy: State the tensor-product indices, weights, denominator, rational basis, map domain and range, map admissibility, and the exact limits of the definition.

items.title: Compactly supported H1 functions lie in H1_0
items.statement: Under Countable Choice, every compactly supported H1 function on an open set belongs to H1_0, proved by zero extension, Meyers–Serrin approximation, and a cutoff.
items.strategy: Extend by zero, approximate in H1 on R^d, multiply by a cutoff equal to one on the compact support, and prove cutoff multiplication preserves H1.

items.title: Tensor Q1 nodal interpolation has a first-order H1 error bound
items.statement: On a uniform degree-one tensor grid in the unit box, the nodal Q1 interpolant of a C1 function with Lipschitz gradient belongs to the tensor spline space and its H1 error is bounded by C_d h Lip(grad g), with an explicit dimension constant.
items.strategy: On each cell subtract the affine Taylor polynomial, use the explicit Q1 nodal shape functions, bound their gradients, and sum cellwise L2 estimates.

items.title: Bi-Lipschitz NURBS maps preserve H1 and energy norms
items.statement: For a finite piecewise C1 bi-Lipschitz NURBS map with j_- <= det DF <= j_+ and bounds on DF and its inverse, pullback is an isomorphism between H1 physical and parametric spaces, preserves H1_0, and transforms gradients and scalar or elasticity energy forms by the inverse-Jacobian and determinant factors.
items.strategy: Prove the estimates for smooth functions cellwise, extend by Meyers-Serrin density and H1 completeness, and pass the weak-gradient identity and zero-boundary closure through compactly supported approximants.

items.title: Matching NURBS patch traces give global H1 conformity
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let a bounded open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, be the union of finitely many bounded knot-cell images with disjoint interiors and a face-to-face finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation. Let $m\ge1$ and let $v: \Omega\to\mathbb R^m$ be $C^1$ on the closure of each cell, with each component's cell gradient square integrable. Suppose the two one-sided vector values agree on every shared face. Then $v\in H^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)$; its weak gradient is the piecewise classical componentwise gradient. This is the interface condition used to form conforming multipatch isogeometric spaces. Boundary conditions remain an additional restriction such as membership in $H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R^m)$.
items.strategy: Test the distributional derivative on a smooth compactly supported function, integrate by parts on each cell, cancel matching interface traces, and identify the remaining L2 cell gradients.

items.title: Positive weights give a bounded partition-of-unity NURBS basis
items.statement: For a finite tensor-product B-spline basis with nonnegative basis functions summing to one and weights w_- <= w_i <= w_+, the NURBS denominator lies in [w_-,w_+], the rational basis is nonnegative and sums to one, its span is S_h/W, and its cellwise derivative has the quotient-rule formula and an explicit weight-dependent bound.
items.strategy: Use products of the one-dimensional partition identities, bound the denominator by a convex combination of weights, then differentiate the quotient on each knot cell.

items.title: Unit-Laplace pullback tensors are Lipschitz in the Jacobian matrix
items.statement: For exact and approximate admissible NURBS maps F and F_h on the same parameter box, with positive Jacobians and operator bounds ||DF||, ||DF_h||, ||DF inverse||, ||DF_h inverse|| <= M and ||DF-DF_h||_Linf <= delta, the unit-diffusion pullback tensors B_F=det(DF) DF^{-1}DF^{-T} and B_Fh differ in operator L infinity norm by at most (d M^(d+1)+2 M^(d+3)) delta.
items.strategy: Use determinant multilinearity, the inverse-matrix difference identity, and a product expansion to bound the transformed tensors.

items.title: NURBS quotient spaces transfer numerator H1 approximation
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $F:\widehat\Omega\to\Omega$ be an admissible NURBS map and $W$ its continuous denominator, with $W\ge w_->0$ and cellwise $G_W:=\|\nabla W\|_{L^\infty}<\infty$. Let $\widehat u$ be real-valued and let $s\in S_h$ be a real numerator spline; assume both are $C^1$ up to the boundary of each cell in the common refinement of the geometry and analysis knot grids, with matching traces, and put $g:=W\widehat u$. Then the physical rational spline $v_h:=(s/W)\circ F^{-1}$ belongs to $H^1(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ and
$$\|u-v_h\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le C_F C_W\|g-s\|_{H^1(\widehat\Omega)},\qquad C_F:=\sqrt{j_+}\sqrt{1+L^2},\quad C_W:=\frac{2}{w_-}+\frac{G_W}{w_-^2},$$
where $u:=\widehat u\circ F^{-1}$. This result transfers a specified numerator approximation bound; it does not assert a polynomial-degree-independent rate or a general $H^1$ rate for arbitrary knot families.
items.strategy: Write u-s/W=(Wu-s)/W and apply the weak product rule and the positive lower bound to control both the value and gradient errors.

references.title: Stefan Takacs, Numerical Analysis of Isogeometric Methods, complete JKU lecture notes, 2018/19

items.title: Matching simplex subdivisions give a NURBS knot-cell geometry interface
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $F,G$ be two admissible tensor-product NURBS maps on $\overline Q=[0,1]^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, with finite knot partitions. Geometry continuity is required even if a representation allows a degree-plus-one interior knot; in particular it follows from degrees $p_r\ge1$ and interior multiplicities $\mu_r\le p_r$. Take the union of all distinct knots in each coordinate, discard zero-length spans, and let $\mathcal C$ be the resulting common rectangular partition. On each closed $C\in\mathcal C$, use the polynomial expressions inherited from the incident open cell, rather than a discontinuous evaluation convention at an endpoint. Their positive denominators, positive Jacobian lower bounds and bounded map/inverse derivatives are required on these expressions. They follow by continuity from uniform cellwise admissibility bounds. No agreement of cross-face normal derivatives is required.

For $C=a+\operatorname{diag}(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_d)[0,1]^d$, subdivide by the $d!$ simplices
$$T_{C,\pi}=\{a+\operatorname{diag}(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_d)t:0\le t_{\pi(1)}\le\cdots\le t_{\pi(d)}\le1\},\qquad \pi\in\mathfrak S_d.$$
These form a matching affine simplicial mesh of $\overline Q$. The restricted maps $F|_{T_{C,\pi}}$ and $G|_{T_{C,\pi}}$ are admissible curved-cell maps in [[def-isoparametric-curved-cell-map]], with the reference simplices taken in parameter coordinates. Their images are matching curved partitions, and the two global maps satisfy [[def-curved-domain-geometry-approximation]] with $\Phi=F$, $\Phi_h=G$, $\Omega=F(Q)$ and $\Omega_h=G(Q)$. The geometry errors are precisely $e_0=\|F-G\|_\infty$ and $e_1=\|DF-DG\|_{L^\infty(\text{cells};op)}$ on the box; subdivision does not change their essential suprema. Matching traces means agreement within each mapped mesh across shared facets, not $F=G$ on the exterior boundary. A prescribed common exterior boundary requires a separate equality of those traces. Common image topology is given by the homeomorphism $G\circ F^{-1}$.

For a sequence of grids, uniform reference-simplex shape regularity follows if $\max_r\ell_r/\min_r\ell_r\le\kappa$ on every rectangle with fixed $\kappa$. Uniform curved-map bounds additionally require uniform first, inverse and second derivative bounds of the rational cell expressions. Finite grids have finite second derivative bounds because denominators stay positive. Neither uniform second derivative bounds nor a shape constant follows from a first derivative error bound alone. The construction changes the geometry presentation only; rational analysis functions remain rational and are not reclassified as affine P1 functions.
items.strategy: Triangulate the common knot-cell rectangles by coordinate order; prove matching faces, local C2 extensions, curved-cell admissibility, and unchanged map errors.

references.title: Guermond, Finite Element Interpolation, Chapter 8, Meshes, complete 12-page chapter, §§8.1–8.2

items.title: Greville comparison splines preserve faces and give an explicit H1 estimate
items.statement:
On $[0,1]^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, choose in coordinate $r$ any finite clamped knot vector $\Xi_r=(\xi^{(r)}_i)$ of degree $p_r\ge1$, with interior multiplicity at most $p_r+1$. Let $h_r$ be its maximum positive span length, $B^{(r)}_i$ its canonical degree-$p_r$ basis, and $t^{(r)}_i=p_r^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^{p_r}\xi^{(r)}_{i+k}$ its Greville points. For a real-valued $g\in C^1([0,1]^d)$ with $M_g$-Lipschitz gradient, define the actual tensor comparison spline
$$\mathcal Sg(x)=\sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}g(t^{(1)}_{i_1},\ldots,t^{(d)}_{i_d})\prod_{r=1}^d B^{(r)}_{i_r}(x_r).$$
Put
$$R=\left(\sum_{r=1}^d(p_r+1)^2h_r^2\right)^{1/2},\qquad E=2\sum_{r=1}^d(2p_r+3)^2h_r^2,\qquad B=E+\sqrt d\,R.$$
Then $\mathcal Sg$ is a continuous tensor spline, including at fully repeated knots, and
$$\|g-\mathcal Sg\|_{L^\infty}\le M_gE,\qquad \|\nabla(g-\mathcal Sg)\|_{L^\infty(\mathrm{cells})}\le\sqrt d\,M_gR.$$
For the Sobolev conclusion assume Countable Choice. Then $\mathcal Sg\in H^1((0,1)^d)$ and $\|g-\mathcal Sg\|_{H^1}\le M_gB$. The finite construction, pointwise cell bounds, continuity and face identities do not use this additional choice assumption.
The operator restricts on a coordinate face to the same construction in the tangential coordinates applied to the face data. Thus it preserves zero face data. If two face grids/degrees agree after coordinate permutation and coordinate reflections $t\mapsto1-t$, their face operators agree under that identification and commute with multiplication of the face data by a constant. No knot-ratio bound is needed. All degree and continuity dependence is retained through the actual knots and the displayed degree factors. This comparison operator need not be idempotent.
items.strategy: Use Greville reproduction and derivative identities with local mean-value estimates; tensorize, then verify repeated-knot continuity and face compatibility.

references.title: Tom Lyche, Carla Manni, and Hendrik Speleers, B-Splines and Spline Approximation

items.title: Homogeneous knot insertion preserves an admissible NURBS patch
items.statement: Inserting one new knot in one coordinate of a finite tensor-product NURBS patch and updating its homogeneous control net by the single-knot B-spline insertion rule leaves the rational geometry map unchanged and leaves every updated weight positive.
items.strategy: Lift each tensor-product control point to homogeneous coordinates, apply the proved curve-preserving insertion to every coefficient slice, and project back using the positive last coordinate.

items.title: Homogeneous NURBS data errors generate geometry and metric error bounds
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $Q=(0,1)^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$. Use a common finite tensor-product B-spline basis $N_\alpha$ of coordinate degrees $p_r\ge1$, clamped endpoint multiplicities $p_r+1$, and interior multiplicities at most $p_r$. Only positive-length knot spans are cells. Exact homogeneous re-representation on this common basis must be established before comparing data on originally different grids; it is not inferred from a common geometric image. Let
$$A=\sum_\alpha a_\alpha N_\alpha,\quad W=\sum_\alpha w_\alpha N_\alpha,\quad F=A/W,\qquad A'=\sum_\alpha a'_\alpha N_\alpha,\quad W'=\sum_\alpha w'_\alpha N_\alpha,\quad G=A'/W'.$$
Here $a_\alpha=w_\alpha P_\alpha\in\mathbb R^d$ and $a'_\alpha=w'_\alpha P'_\alpha$. Suppose $F$ is admissible in [[def-nurbs-patch-map-and-rational-spline-space]], $w_-\le w_\alpha\le w_+$, $\|DF\|,\|(DF)^{-1}\|\le L$, $\det DF\ge j_->0$, and the global lower Lipschitz bound is explicitly $|F(x)-F(y)|\ge c|x-y|$ on $\overline Q$, $c>0$. The latter is the reciprocal of a global inverse Lipschitz bound and need not equal $1/L$.

Define finite data quantities
$$\epsilon_A=\max_\alpha|a'_\alpha-a_\alpha|,\quad \epsilon_W=\max_\alpha|w'_\alpha-w_\alpha|<w_-,\quad m=w_--\epsilon_W>0,\quad R=\max_\alpha|P_\alpha|,$$
$$H=\sum_\alpha\max_C\|\nabla N_\alpha\|_{L^\infty(C)},\quad T=\epsilon_A+R\epsilon_W,\qquad E_0=T/m,$$
$$E_1=\frac{H\epsilon_A+L\epsilon_W+RH\epsilon_W}{m}+\frac{T(w_++\epsilon_W)H}{m^2}.$$
All vector norms are Euclidean and all derivative norms are operator norms. $H$ is defined by the actual cell polynomials, so retains every degree, knot-spacing and multiplicity dependence. It is finite on each fixed finite nondegenerate grid; no uniform bound over degenerating grids is asserted. Then $w'_\alpha\ge m$, $G$ is continuous on $\overline Q$, and
$$e_0:=\|F-G\|_\infty\le E_0,\qquad e_1:=\|DF-DG\|_{L^\infty(\text{cells};op)}\le E_1.$$
If $E_1<\min(c,1/L)$, then $G$ is globally injective and bi-Lipschitz onto its image, and
$$|G(x)-G(y)|\ge(c-E_1)|x-y|,\quad \|DG\|\le L+E_1,\quad \|(DG)^{-1}\|\le\frac{L}{1-LE_1},\quad \det DG\ge j_-(1-LE_1)^d>0.$$
The image $G(Q)$ is open. For the admissible-patch conclusion, retain the explicit boundary hypothesis that $G(Q)$ is a Lipschitz domain with its finite piecewise $C^1$ knot-cell presentation. A sufficient verifiable alternative is that $G$ extends $C^1$ to a neighborhood of $\overline Q$ with nonsingular derivative there; this alternative holds when every interior multiplicity is at most $p_r-1$. With either boundary condition $G$ is admissible. No equality of the physical boundaries of $F(Q)$ and $G(Q)$ is asserted; their correspondence is $G\circ F^{-1}$.

For these admissible maps put
$$M=\max\left(1,L,L+E_1,\frac{L}{1-LE_1}\right),\qquad C_M=dM^{d+1}+2M^{d+3}.$$
Their unit-Laplace tensors satisfy $\|K_F-K_G\|_\infty\le C_ME_1$, and their bilinear-form difference is at most $C_ME_1\|\nabla v\|_2\|\nabla w\|_2$. For any family with uniformly bounded $L,c^{-1},R,w_+,m^{-1}$ and $H\epsilon_A+H\epsilon_W+\epsilon_W=O(h^s)$, $s>0$, the geometry form defect is $O(h^s)$. The bound is generated from homogeneous data; convergence of those data remains a separate approximation or certification obligation. Loads, quadrature and boundary-lift defects remain separate.

A concrete geometry generator is scalar rounding of every component of $a_\alpha$ and every $w_\alpha$ to the nearest multiple of $2^{-b}$ (ties go to the smaller integer), followed by $P'_\alpha=a'_\alpha/w'_\alpha$. Put $\eta_b=2^{-b-1}$ and
$$D=\frac{2H\sqrt d+2L+2RH}{w_-}+\frac{4(\sqrt d+R)(w_++w_-/2)H}{w_-^2}.$$
Choose an integer $b\ge0$ such that $\eta_b<\min(w_-/2,c/(2D),1/(2LD))$. Then this generator has $\epsilon_A\le\sqrt d\,\eta_b$, $\epsilon_W\le\eta_b$, $e_0\le2(\sqrt d+R)\eta_b/w_-$, and $e_1\le D\eta_b$; in particular it generates the positive denominator, Jacobian, and global injectivity bounds above. In the $C^1$ knot branch ($\mu_r\le p_r-1$) it generates admissible approximate domains without an independent boundary certificate. Taking $b$ so that $D\eta_b\le h^s$ produces a stated geometry derivative rate for any supplied grid family, with its actual $D$, rather than claiming a rate from positive weights or knot refinement alone.
items.strategy: Derive value and derivative errors from homogeneous coefficient changes, establish global bi-Lipschitz stability and the boundary branches, then propagate tensor and dyadic bounds.

items.title: Conforming isogeometric Galerkin spaces and h/p/k refinement
items.statement:
For one admissible patch map $F:\widehat\Omega\to\Omega$, let $S_h$ be a finite tensor-product B-spline space on a knot grid refining the geometry grid, and let $W$ be the positive denominator of the geometry representation. The parametric rational analysis space is
$$\widehat V_h:=\{s/W:s\in S_h\}.$$
Its physical push-forward is $\{\,\widehat v\circ F^{-1}:\widehat v\in\widehat V_h\,\}$. The homogeneous-Dirichlet conforming space is the subspace of these functions that belongs to $H^1_0(\Omega)$; the unconstrained conforming version is the subspace belonging to $H^1(\Omega)$. These spaces are finite dimensional because the tensor B-spline coefficient set is finite.

For vector-valued elasticity in $\mathbb R^d$, use the componentwise product $\widehat V_h^{\,d}:=(\widehat V_h)^d$, push it forward component by component, and intersect with $H^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$ or $H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$ as appropriate. This remains finite dimensional because it is a subspace of the finite product of scalar coefficient spaces. Trace equality is required componentwise on each shared full face.

For finitely many matching patches, use one such local rational space on each patch. A global trial function is a piecewise physical function whose traces agree pointwise on every shared full face and which belongs to the chosen global $H^1$ or $H^1_0$ space. Under [[def-countable-choice|Countable Choice]], the vector-valued trace-matching lemma [[lem-matching-nurbs-patch-traces-give-h1-conformity]] proves the H1 part of this interface rule componentwise, including the Cartesian product used for elasticity. Nonmatching interfaces are excluded; a mortar or Nitsche method requires a separate stability and consistency result.

The refinement labels have the following meanings.

- **h-refinement** inserts a new knot into a nonempty span at fixed degree and updates homogeneous control data by [[alg-single-new-b-spline-knot-insertion]]. Theorem [[thm-homogeneous-nurbs-knot-insertion-preserves-patch-geometry]] proves exact map preservation for this operation.
- **p-refinement** raises a coordinate degree and replaces the homogeneous representation only when an exact representation with positive new weights is supplied. A degree label alone does not certify geometry preservation or an approximation rate.
- **k-refinement** raises degree and chooses knot multiplicities to obtain a declared continuity, commonly the maximal $C^{p_r-1}$ continuity at simple interior knots. Exact geometry preservation requires the same positive homogeneous representation check as p-refinement.

On each cell, the pullback of scalar gradients and of the linear-elasticity strain is computed using [[lem-isogeometric-pullback-energy-norm-equivalence]]. Exact geometry does not assert exact quadrature. A discretization using an approximate map or quadrature must retain its separate form and load defects.
items.strategy: Specify the finite-dimensional coefficient spaces, trace compatibility across matching interfaces, the H1_0 restriction, and the distinct geometric obligations for h, p, and k changes.

items.title: Finite-Lamé isogeometric elasticity is conforming and quasi-optimal
items.statement: For the homogeneous-Dirichlet isotropic small-strain elasticity model in dimensions two or three, every finite Lamé parameter lambda >= 0 and every finite-dimensional conforming isogeometric displacement space have a unique exact-integral Galerkin solution with the explicit (2 mu_1 + d lambda)/mu_0 best-approximation factor. No lambda-uniform bound is asserted.
items.strategy: Match the homogeneous Dirichlet model and finite-dimensional conforming trial-space hypotheses exactly, then apply the current Batch 35 elasticity Galerkin theorem.

items.title: Isogeometric geometry and quadrature defects enter through Strang's bound
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and use real scalar Sobolev spaces. Let $\widehat\Omega=(0,1)^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, and $V=H^1_0(\widehat\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with the gradient norm. Let $F$ be an exact admissible patch map and $G$ an approximate admissible map on the same reference box, with a common finite refinement of their cell grids. Let $f$ be a bounded real-linear functional on $H^1_0(F(\widehat\Omega);\mathbb R)$ equipped with its physical gradient norm, and define the exact pulled-back unit-diffusion form and load by
$$\widehat a_F(v,w)=\int_{\widehat\Omega}K_F\nabla v\cdot\nabla w,\quad K_F=(\det DF)DF^{-1}DF^{-\mathsf T},\qquad \widehat\ell_F(w)=\langle f,w\circ F^{-1}\rangle.$$
Define $\widehat a_G$ by the same tensor formula with $G$. Let $u\in V$ solve $\widehat a_F(u,w)=\widehat\ell_F(w)$ for every $w\in V$. Let $V_h\subset V$ be a finite conforming rational spline space and let bounded $a_h$ and $\ell_h$ be a discrete form and load assembled using $G$ and a specified quadrature rule. Assume $a_h$ is coercive on $V_h$ with inherited norm and constant $\alpha_h>0$, and let $M_F$ be a boundedness constant for $\widehat a_F$. Define
$$\delta_{\rm geom}(v_h):=\sup_{w_h\ne0}\frac{|\widehat a_F(v_h,w_h)-\widehat a_G(v_h,w_h)|}{\|w_h\|_V},\quad \delta_{\rm quad}(v_h):=\sup_{w_h\ne0}\frac{|\widehat a_G(v_h,w_h)-a_h(v_h,w_h)|}{\|w_h\|_V},$$
and $\delta_{\rm load}:=\sup_{w_h\ne0}|\widehat\ell_F(w_h)-\ell_h(w_h)|/\|w_h\|_V$. When $V_h=\{0\}$ define all three defects to be zero. Let $u_h\in V_h$ solve the discrete problem; then
$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\left((1+M_F/\alpha_h)\|u-v_h\|_V+\frac{\delta_{\rm geom}(v_h)+\delta_{\rm quad}(v_h)+\delta_{\rm load}}{\alpha_h}\right).$$
If $\delta=\|DF-DG\|_{L^\infty({\rm op})}$ and both map derivative and inverse bounds are at most $M\ge1$, then the geometry defect obeys
$$\delta_{\rm geom}(v_h)\le(dM^{d+1}+2M^{d+3})\delta\,\|v_h\|_V.$$
The hypotheses require discrete coercivity; neither exact geometry nor positive NURBS weights imply it. The estimate retains the load defect and makes no convergence claim for any geometry or quadrature rule.
items.strategy: Pull the exact problem to the common parameter domain, split the form defect into geometry and quadrature parts, retain the load defect, and apply the published first Strang estimate.

items.statement: For a bounded coercive scalar diffusion form on a bounded Lipschitz patch domain and every finite-dimensional conforming isogeometric subspace V_h subset H1_0, the exact-integral Galerkin solution is unique and satisfies the M/alpha best-approximation bound in the H1_0 norm.

items.title: Tensorized spline quasi-interpolation gives a NURBS L2 rate
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. On each coordinate interval $[0,1]$, let a clamped degree-$p_r$ analysis knot mesh have largest cell size $h_r$, and let $Q_r$ be a family as in [[def-local-spline-quasi-interpolant]] with reproduction order $0\le\ell_r\le p_r$, local constant $M_r$, and stability constant $C_r$. Require each analysis knot mesh to refine the corresponding geometry knot vector, and let $S_h=\bigotimes_{r=1}^d S_{p_r,\xi^{(r)}}$ be the corresponding numerator space defining the patch trial space in [[def-isogeometric-galerkin-patch-space-and-refinement]]. Suppose $g:\widehat\Omega\to\mathbb R$ belongs to $L^2(\widehat\Omega)$, has weak pure derivatives $\partial_r^{\ell_r+1}g\in L^2(\widehat\Omega)$, and, for each $r$, almost every section in coordinate $r$ belongs to $W^{\ell_r+1,2}(0,1)$ and satisfies the hypotheses of the one-dimensional estimate in [[thm-sobolev-spline-quasi-interpolant-rate]]. Require each $Q_r$ to have its bounded extension to $L^2(\widehat\Omega)$, acting in coordinate $r$, with norm at most $S_r=C_r\sqrt{M_r}$; require the coordinate operators to commute pairwise and to commute with weak derivatives in every other coordinate on this class. These are explicit hypotheses on the supplied family, not conclusions of the univariate rate theorem. Under the Axiom of Choice, completed-product Fubini is available, and the sectionwise operators and derivatives are assumed measurable. Define $\mathcal Q:=Q_d\cdots Q_1$ and set $A_r:=(1+C_r)M_r^{\ell_r+1+1/2}/\ell_r!$. Then $\mathcal Qg\in S_h$ and
$$\|g-\mathcal Qg\|_{L^2(\widehat\Omega)} \le\sum_{r=1}^d A_r\!\left(\prod_{j\ne r}S_j\right)h_r^{\ell_r+1}\|\partial_r^{\ell_r+1}g\|_{L^2(\widehat\Omega)}.$$
If $g=W(\widehat u)$ and $v_h:=(\mathcal Qg/W)\circ F^{-1}$, then
$$\|u-v_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le \frac{\sqrt{j_+}}{w_-}\|g-\mathcal Qg\|_{L^2(\widehat\Omega)},\qquad u:=\widehat u\circ F^{-1}.$$
This is an $L^2$ approximation estimate. It does not imply an $H^1$ energy rate.
items.strategy: Tensorize the coordinate operators, prove their L2 stability by summing local bounds with finite overlap, telescope I minus the product, and transfer the numerator estimate through W and F.

items.title: Smooth compactly supported data have a degree-one NURBS energy rate
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $F:\widehat\Omega\to D$ be one admissible NURBS patch, $\widehat\Omega=(0,1)^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, with determinant upper bound $j_+$, derivative and inverse-derivative bound $L$, and continuous denominator $W$ that is $C^1$ on each knot cell, satisfies $W\ge w_->0$, and has $\|\nabla W\|_{L^\infty}\le G_W$. Let $g\in C^1(\overline{\widehat\Omega})$ have Lipschitz gradient with constant $M_g$ and support contained in a nonempty compact set $K\Subset\widehat\Omega$, and set $\widehat u=g/W$ and $u=\widehat u\circ F^{-1}$. Let the uniform tensor grid of side $h=1/N$ refine the geometry knot grid, let $S_h$ be its tensor-product degree-one $C^0$ numerator space, and let $V_h=\{(s/W)\circ F^{-1}:s\in S_h\}\cap H^1_0(D)$ be the corresponding isogeometric trial space. Let $I_hg$ be the tensor Q1 nodal interpolant. If $h<\operatorname{dist}(K,\partial\widehat\Omega)/\sqrt d$, then $v_h=(I_hg/W)\circ F^{-1}$ belongs to $V_h$. If $u$ is the weak solution of an exact symmetric scalar elliptic problem with coefficient operator bound $\beta$ and coercivity bound $\alpha$ as in [[thm-isogeometric-poisson-galerkin-quasioptimality]], and $u_h$ its exact-form isogeometric Galerkin solution in $V_h$, then
$$\|u-u_h\|_{H^1_0(D),\nabla}\le\frac\beta\alpha\,C_F C_W C_d\,hM_g,$$
where $C_F=\sqrt{j_+}\sqrt{1+L^2}$, $C_W=2/w_-+G_W/w_-^2$, and $C_d=d+\sqrt d+2^{d-1}d\sqrt d$. These constants retain their map, weight, coefficient, and dimension dependence. This proves only the degree-one compact-support branch; it is not a general high-degree, knot-family, or locking-free rate.
items.strategy: Use tensor Q1 nodal interpolation of the numerator, reproduce its affine Taylor polynomial on each cell, bound derivative errors by the Hessian supremum, transfer through W and F, and apply Céa.

items.title: Boundary-preserving NURBS projection and matching-patch energy approximation
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and use real-valued scalar Sobolev spaces throughout. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, be a nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz domain with a finite face-to-face admissible NURBS patch partition as in [[def-isogeometric-galerkin-patch-space-and-refinement]]. Let $V_h\subset H^1_0(D;\mathbb R)$ be its full finite rational trial space with matching physical traces and homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition. For any such finite space, including the zero space, there is a real-linear projector $\Pi_h:H^1_0(D;\mathbb R)\to V_h$ specified by
$$\int_D\bigl(\Pi_hu\,v_h+\nabla\Pi_hu\cdot\nabla v_h\bigr)=\int_D\bigl(u v_h+\nabla u\cdot\nabla v_h\bigr)\qquad(v_h\in V_h).$$
It fixes every $v_h\in V_h$, satisfies $\Pi_h^2=\Pi_h$, preserves the homogeneous boundary condition for every $H^1_0$ input, and
$$\|\Pi_hu\|_{H^1(D)}\le\|u\|_{H^1(D)},\qquad \|u-\Pi_hu\|_{H^1(D)}\le\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_{H^1(D)}.$$
This is a global variational projector, defined without point evaluation of $H^1$ inputs.

For the following actual approximation estimate, on patch $a$ let $F_a$ have determinant upper bound $j_{+,a}$ and inverse/forward derivative bound $L_a$, and let its fixed continuous positive geometry denominator satisfy $W_a\ge w_{-,a}>0$ and $\|\nabla W_a\|_{L^\infty(\mathrm{cells})}\le G_a$. Require the analysis knot grids defining $V_h$ to refine the geometry knot grids. Choose the tensor clamped analysis knots defining the local numerator spaces of $V_h$ with degrees $p_{a,r}\ge1$, maximum spans $h_{a,r}$, and interior multiplicities at most $p_{a,r}+1$; require their numerator spaces to contain the geometry numerator and denominator after any exact re-representation. Use $R_a,E_a,B_a$ from [[lem-boundary-preserving-tensor-schoenberg-h1-approximation]] for these actual knots.

For each shared face, require its parameter identification to be a permutation and reflections of tangential coordinates, its tangential degrees and knot vectors to agree under that identification, and
$$W_a|_f=c_{ab}\,W_b|_{f'}\circ T_{ab}\quad\text{for a specified constant }c_{ab}>0.$$
These are explicit sufficient compatibility data for the approximation branch, checked on finite face representations; a single patch needs none. For $u\in H^1_0(D)$ require $g_a:=W_a(u\circ F_a)$ to have a $C^1$ representative on the closed reference box with $M_a$-Lipschitz gradient, to vanish on every exterior face, and to satisfy $g_a|_f=c_{ab}g_b|_{f'}\circ T_{ab}$ on each shared face. These pointwise conditions concern only this smooth approximation class. Define
$$C_a=\sqrt{j_{+,a}}\sqrt{1+L_a^2}\left(\frac2{w_{-,a}}+\frac{G_a}{w_{-,a}^2}\right),\qquad \varepsilon_h=\left(\sum_a C_a^2 M_a^2B_a^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
Then the explicitly constructed $v_h|_{F_a((0,1)^d)}=(\mathcal S_ag_a/W_a)\circ F_a^{-1}$ belongs to $V_h$ and
$$\|u-\Pi_hu\|_{H^1(D)}\le\|u-v_h\|_{H^1(D)}\le\varepsilon_h.$$
For fixed bounded degrees and uniform map/weight/numerator bounds this is an $O(\max_{a,r}h_{a,r})$ H1 estimate on arbitrary graded meshes, including simple-knot maximal-continuity families. If degrees vary with refinement, retain the actual $B_a$; convergence follows whenever the displayed $\varepsilon_h$ tends to zero. This does not assert an optimal $h^{p}$ rate or a degree-independent constant.

Under the exact scalar elliptic data of [[thm-isogeometric-poisson-galerkin-quasioptimality]], its Galerkin solution obeys $\|u-u_h\|_{\nabla}\le(\beta/\alpha)\varepsilon_h$. Componentwise the same construction applies to finite-Lamé elasticity: if $M_{a,q}$ bounds the gradient Lipschitz constant of component numerator $q$, replace $M_a^2$ by $\sum_qM_{a,q}^2$ in $\varepsilon_h^2$ and obtain $\|u-u_h\|_{\nabla}\le(2\mu_1+d\lambda)\mu_0^{-1}\varepsilon_h$ under that supplier's full data.

For the single-patch reference-domain problem in [[thm-isogeometric-perturbed-geometry-quadrature-strang-bound]], assume $g=Wu$ satisfies the same $C^{1,1}$ and zero-boundary conditions above. Apply the construction with the reference-domain projector $\Pi_h$ and put $\widehat\varepsilon_h=(2/w_-+G/w_-^2)M_gB$. Then its original defects and constants give
$$\|u-u_h\|_{\nabla}\le(1+M_F/\alpha_h)\widehat\varepsilon_h+\alpha_h^{-1}\bigl(\delta_{\rm geom}(\Pi_hu)+\delta_{\rm quad}(\Pi_hu)+\delta_{\rm load}\bigr).$$
In particular its existing geometry bound gives $\delta_{\rm geom}(\Pi_hu)\le(dM^{d+1}+2M^{d+3})\|DF-DG\|_\infty\|u\|_{H^1}$; discrete coercivity, load error and quadrature error remain separate hypotheses/terms.
items.strategy: Use full-H1 Céa for the orthogonal projector; construct a compatible Greville numerator approximation, prove its zero-boundary membership, and transfer patchwise H1 errors.

items.title: Positive NURBS weights do not imply an admissible patch
items.statement: A bilinear tensor-product patch with all weights equal to one can have a zero and sign-changing Jacobian and can fail global injectivity.
items.strategy: Give the four control points for F(xi,eta)=(xi,eta(1-2xi)), compute its determinant, and exhibit distinct parameters with the same image.

items.title: A tensor NURBS patch exactly covers a quarter annulus
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Fix $0<r_0<1$. Use a linear radial coordinate $\rho(s)=r_0+(1-r_0)s$ and a rational quadratic angular curve with control points $Q_0=(1,0)$, $Q_1=(1,1)$, $Q_2=(0,1)$ and weights $(1,1/\sqrt2,1)$. Tensor their bases, use control points $P_{ij}=r_iQ_j$ for $r_i\in\{r_0,1\}$, and tensor weights $w_{ij}=w_j$. The resulting patch maps $[0,1]^2$ bijectively onto $\{(x,y):r_0\le\sqrt{x^2+y^2}\le1,\ x,y\ge0\}$ with strictly positive Jacobian, and its exact map satisfies the norm-equivalence hypotheses of [[lem-isogeometric-pullback-energy-norm-equivalence]].
items.strategy: Compute the rational quadratic arc, verify the unit-circle identity and strict angular monotonicity, then compute the radial-angular Jacobian.

items.title: Matching patch geometry does not repair a field trace jump
items.statement: Two identity NURBS patches with adjacent physical images and a unit jump in the field trace across their common face define a piecewise rational field that is not in H1 of the union.
items.strategy: Integrate by parts on the two rectangles to identify the interface measure in the distributional derivative, then use a concentrating test-function sequence to rule out an L2 weak derivative.

items.title: Degree elevation and simple-knot insertion preserve the identity patch
items.statement: A degree-one tensor-product identity patch can be represented exactly after degree elevation to degree two and insertion of simple midpoint knots, producing C1 continuity without changing its geometry.
items.strategy: Verify the degree-two Bernstein representation of each coordinate, then apply the homogeneous knot-insertion preservation theorem in each coordinate.
